text: {"findings":[{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"No experiment plan; full rollout with no control","detail":"The proposal launches to all markets and only monitors a dashboard, with no randomization, control group, MDE, power analysis, or duration. A before/after comparison can't separate the incentive effect from seasonality or other changes.","evidence_quote":"None. We will roll out to all markets and monitor the dashboard.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Design a randomized test (e.g., by zone-time or market with spillover controls) running at least 14 days, with a defined MDE and power calculation, and a holdout before any full rollout."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Driver pay change without required review","detail":"A surge incentive changes driver compensation, which is a pay-controlled area. The Reviews section says 'None', so no pay/compensation, legal, or finance review is recorded.","evidence_quote":"Launch a surge incentive during peak hours across all markets and watch the dashboard.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record compensation/pay policy, legal, and finance review before launch, including market-specific pay regulations."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for incentive spend, cost, and delivery quality","detail":"The only guardrail is acceptance rate in neighboring zones, which is vague. There are no guardrails on incentive cost per order, unassigned order rate, delivery time/late deliveries, or order cancellation, and no cannibalization of non-peak supply.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate in neighboring zones: should not drop.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as incentive cost per delivery, delivery time/on-time rate, order cancellation rate, and off-peak supply, each with numeric thresholds."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Guardrail lacks numeric threshold; success metric misaligned with problem","detail":"The guardrail 'should not drop' has no baseline, numeric tolerance, or timeframe. The problem is unassigned orders, yet the success metric does not measure that outcome.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate in neighboring zones: should not drop.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Specify a baseline and a maximum allowed drop (e.g., no more than X pp over the test window), and add a success metric tied to unassigned order rate or supply coverage with baseline, target, and timeframe."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Ambiguous metric definition for evening supply problem","detail":"The problem is framed as 'short supply' and 'unassigned orders' without a defined metric. 'Peak hours' and 'neighboring zones' are also not defined, making the metric scope ambiguous.","evidence_quote":"Evening driver supply is short, leaving orders unassigned.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use canonical glossary metrics (e.g., unassigned order rate, driver supply hours) and define the peak-hour window and neighboring zone scope."}]}
